## 1. Fire Access Roads (Fire Lanes)

### REQ-01: Fire Access Distance
- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All projects with buildings

- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Fire department access roads within 150 ft of all exterior points of non-sprinkled buildings
  - Fire department access roads within 200 ft of all exterior points of sprinkled buildings
  - Distance measured as hose lay at ground level around obstructions
  - Distance cannot be measured under or through buildings
- **Common Failures**:
  - Courtyards without fire access
  - Rear of buildings beyond allowed distance

  - Not accounting for fences as obstructions

- **Example Comments**:

### REQ-02: Fire Lane Width
- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All fire lanes
- **Code references**: IFC 503.2.1
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Minimum 25 ft wide for two-way fire lanes
  - Minimum 20 ft wide for one-way non-dead-end streets
  - Minimum 14 ft vertical clearance
- **Common Failures**:
  - Fire lanes measuring 21-24 ft instead of 25 ft
  - Obstructions reducing clear width
  - Power lines below 14 ft clearance
- **Detection/Evidence**: Scale fire lane width at multiple points; check callouts match actual dimensions
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Fire Department access roads must be a minimum of 25 ft wide with a minimum of 14 ft vertical clearance. IFC 503.2.1"
  - "Portions of fire lane are shown to be 24ft, this includes portions where there is no curb and gutter shown only the FL line type"
  - "Please verify 14 feet clear height for fire lane under power lines."

- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All fire lane turns
- **Code references**: IFC 503.2.4
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - 50 ft outside turning radius
  - 25 ft inside turning radius
  - Building footprint cannot fall within turning radii

  - Buildings encroaching into turning area

- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All dead-end fire lanes
- **Code references**: IFC 503.2.5, Fire Criteria Manual Appendix G
- **Pass Criteria**:

  - Turnaround complies with City of Austin approved designs
  - See Fire Criteria Manual Appendix G for approved turnarounds
- **Common Failures**:

- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All fire lanes
- **Code references**: IFC 503.2.3, IFC 503.2.6, IFC 503.2.7

- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All projects
- **Code references**: IFC 507.5.1
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Non-sprinkled buildings: 1 hydrant within 400 ft of all exterior wall portions
  - Sprinkled buildings (13 or 13R): 1 hydrant within 500 ft
  - Townhomes with 13D: 1 hydrant within 600 ft
  - Distance measured as hose lay at ground level
- **Common Failures**:
  - Portions of building beyond hydrant reach
  - Measuring through building or obstructions
  - Using hydrant across divided highway
- **Detection/Evidence**: Measure scaled distance from hydrants to all building wall points
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Fire hydrant locations. AFD requires a minimum of 1 hydrant within 400 ft of all portions of exterior walls. A second hydrant is required within 500 ft if the fire flow is 1500 gpm or more. IFC 507.5.1"
  - "EXCEPTION: For sprinklered buildings (13 or 13R) the first hydrant can be 500 ft and the second must also be within 500 ft."

### REQ-09: Secondary Hydrant Distance
- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: Projects with fire flow ≥ 1500 gpm
- **Code references**: IFC 507.5.1
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Second hydrant within 500 ft of all exterior wall portions
  - Hydrant across divided highway not acceptable as secondary
  - Hydrant across major/primary roadway not acceptable (hose lay policy)
- **Common Failures**:
  - Only one hydrant shown when fire flow ≥ 1500 gpm
  - Relying on hydrant across major roadway
  - Secondary hydrant location not shown
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check fire flow demand; count hydrants within 500 ft
- **Example Comments**:
  - "A second hydrant is required within 500 ft of all portions of exterior walls if the fire flow is 1500 gpm or more."
  - "AFD does not lay water supply hose lines across major or primary roadways in the area and hydrants on the other side of a major or primary roadway from a site cannot be used to meet this requirement."

### REQ-10: Hydrant Location Requirements
- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All hydrants
- **Code references**: IFC 507.5.1.1, NFPA 24-7.2.3, Fire Criteria Manual
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Hydrant directly adjacent to fire lane or public street
  - Steamer (4") opening faces fire access
  - Center of steamer 18" above finished grade
  - Setback 3-6 ft from curb line
  - 3 ft clear in all directions from hydrant
  - Hydrant not in collapse zone (40 ft from building corner)
  - Hydrant not in pond slopes or detention areas
- **Common Failures**:
  - Hydrant not adjacent to fire lane
  - Hydrant in detention pond slope
  - Hydrant in building collapse zone
  - Access to hydrant requires going through building/breezeway
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check hydrant proximity to fire lanes; identify obstructions
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Fire Hydrants are required to be directly adjacent to either the Fire Lane or Public Street"
  - "Please locate fire hydrant out of pond slope and next to a fire lane."
  - "The proposed hydrant near Building #6 is not in an approved location. It is currently located within the collapse zone of the structure and needs to be relocated away from the structure by at least 40 feet. NFPA 24-Section 7.2.3"

### REQ-11: Private Hydrant Identification
- **Frequency**: Frequently
- **When it applies**: Projects with private fire hydrants
- **Code references**: AFD requirement
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Private hydrants clearly identified as "Private" in callouts
  - Note on plans: "All private hydrants shall be painted red."
  - Private hydrants must be in PUE or on private property
- **Common Failures**:
  - No distinction between public and private hydrants
  - Missing red paint note
  - Private hydrant note when hydrants are in ROW (public)
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check hydrant locations vs property lines and easements
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Utility Plan – there are private fire hydrants on the site, clearly call them out as Private in the callouts and provide the following note on the plans: 'All private hydrants shall be painted red.'"

## 3. Fire Flow Analysis

### REQ-12: Fire Hydrant Flow Test
- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All projects
- **Code references**: IFC 507.4 (Local Amendment), Fire Criteria Manual Appendix E
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - AFD flow test required (not third party)
  - Test within 1 year of submittal (some comments allow 3 years)
  - Both pages of test report submitted
  - Test location at or near point of connection
  - Flow test date and location shown on cover sheet
- **Common Failures**:
  - No flow test provided
  - Flow test expired (over 1 year old)
  - Only one page of test provided
  - Test location far from tie-in point
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check for flow test in plan set; verify date
- **Example Comments**:
  - "An AFD flow test that is 1yr old or less must be obtained and both pages submitted to demonstrate the available water supply for the project can meet the fire flow demand for the site."
  - "The flow test provided is not near the tie in point. Suggest getting a flow test at the tie in point."
  - "Fire flow test provided on the cover page is too old. Provide a new fire flow test for the property."

### REQ-13: Fire Flow Demand Calculation
- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All projects
- **Code references**: IFC 507.1, IFC Appendix B (Table B105.1, B105.2)
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Fire flow based on worst-case (most demanding) building
  - Fire area = total floor area of all floor levels within exterior walls plus horizontal roof projections
  - Fire flow calculated per IFC Table B105.1(2) for commercial; B105.1(1) for residential
  - Correct construction classification used
  - Fire flow shown on cover sheet before deductions
- **Common Failures**:
  - Wrong fire area (not including all floors)
  - Wrong construction type
  - Using reduced fire flow as "required fire flow"
  - Fire area doesn't match between tables
- **Detection/Evidence**: Calculate fire flow from building area and construction type
- **Example Comments**:
  - "The fire-flow calculation area shall be the total floor area of all floor levels within the exterior walls, and under the horizontal projections of the roof of a building. (IFC B104.1)"
  - "The gross square footage on the site plan data table is larger than the proposed fire area on the coversheet. Revise fire area and fire flow demand to the correct value."
  - "Cover Sheet – revise Fire Department Information Table - Required Fire Flow before deductions, per 2021 IFC, Table B105.1(2)"

### REQ-14: Sprinkler Fire Flow Reduction
- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: Sprinkled buildings
- **Code references**: IFC Table B105.2
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - NFPA 13 (full sprinkler): up to 75% reduction, minimum 1000 gpm
  - NFPA 13R: up to 50% reduction, minimum 1500 gpm (Type V combustible construction limits to 50%)
  - NFPA 13D: see Table B105.1(1) for residential
  - Non-combustible construction (IA, IB, IIA): 75% reduction allowed
  - Combustible construction (V): 50% reduction maximum
- **Common Failures**:
  - Claiming 75% reduction with 13R system
  - Claiming 75% reduction with Type V construction
  - Reduced fire flow below allowed minimum
  - Wrong sprinkler system type indicated
- **Detection/Evidence**: Verify construction type allows claimed reduction; check sprinkler type
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Fire flow reduction is allowed up to 75% for non combustible construction. The plan indicated type 5A construction which is combustible. Please revise the allowed reduction to 50%"
  - "At 1000gpm only (1) hydrant is required to be within 500ft of all portions of the buildings. It is only when the sprinkler system is a NFPA 13R that the min allowed fire flow is 1500gpm"

### REQ-15: Available Fire Flow Verification
- **Frequency**: Frequently
- **When it applies**: All projects
- **Code references**: IFC 507.1, Fire Criteria Manual
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Available fire flow at 20 psi meets or exceeds required demand
  - AWU evaluates impacts to piping system
  - Maximum velocity 10 ft/second in public and private fire mains
- **Common Failures**:
  - Available fire flow calculation incorrect
  - Static pressure discrepancy between test and tables
  - Velocity exceeds 10 fps
- **Detection/Evidence**: Calculate available fire flow from test data
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Based on the fire hydrant flow test report, it appears that adequate fire flow is available to meet the 1500 gpm fire flow demand for this project. However, impacts to the Austin Water Utility (AWU) piping system due to providing the required fire flow for a development project are evaluated by and resolved through the staff of AWU. The maximum allowable flow velocity permitted in the public fire mains is 10 feet/second."

### REQ-16: Private Hydrant Hydraulic Calculations
- **Frequency**: Frequently
- **When it applies**: Projects with private fire hydrants
- **Code references**: Fire Criteria Manual, NFPA 24
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Calculations sealed by TX Licensed PE
  - Show all hydrants needed to meet fire flow flowing simultaneously
  - Minimum 20 psi residual pressure maintained
  - Maximum 10 fps velocity in mains (allowed to exceed in 6" hydrant lead only)
  - Maximum 1250 gpm per hydrant
  - Show pipe sizes, fittings, valves, nodes, network schematic
  - Use AWU-approved C-factors (110 for PVC, 80 for ductile iron)
- **Common Failures**:
  - Missing calculations for private hydrants
  - Calculations not sealed
  - Incorrect C-factors
  - Not showing all required variables
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check for sealed hydraulic calculations in plan set
- **Example Comments**:
  - "For private hydrants the engineer shall provide sealed calculations that demonstrate the hydrants can meet the required fire flow demand... All hydrants required to meet the fire flow demand flowing simultaneously. The minimum residual pressure cannot be less than 20psi anywhere in the system. The velocity in the mains cannot exceed 10ft/s."
  - "Hydraulic calculations must be signed and sealed by a State of Texas Registered Professional Engineer and must utilize the C-factors set forth in the City of Austin Fire Protection Criteria Manual."

- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All sprinkled buildings

    6. Automatic Fire Sprinkler System Type (NFPA 13/13R/13D)
    7. Reduced Fire Flow Demand @ 20 psi (with minimums)
    8. AFD Fire Hydrant Flow Test Date
    9. AFD Fire Hydrant Flow Test Location
    10. High-Rise (Yes/No)
    11. Alternative Method of Compliance (AMOC number and date)
- **Common Failures**:
  - Wrong or missing IFC year
  - Occupancy classification instead of construction classification
  - Fire flow shown after reductions instead of before
  - Missing sprinkler system type
  - Missing AMOC reference when applicable
  - Available fire flow incorrectly calculated
- **Detection/Evidence**: Compare cover sheet table to required format
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Cover sheet – fire flow table, per 2015 IFC table B105.2, the reduced fire flow after sprinkler reduction for full NFPA 13 system, can be lowered to 1000gpm"
  - "Construction classification – what is shown is an 'occupancy classification' not a construction classification – revise."
  - "Revise the Fire Flow demand to state the full required fire flow 'before' any deductions are taken for a sprinkler system."

### REQ-29: Site Plan Number on All Sheets
- **Frequency**: Frequently
- **When it applies**: All sheets
- **Code references**: AFD requirement
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Full SP number shown on all sheets
- **Common Failures**:
  - Missing SP number on some sheets
  - Incorrect SP number
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check each sheet for SP number
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Provide the full site plan number on all sheets."
  - "Current submission does not have the SP number on any sheets."

### REQ-30: Fire Department Notes
- **Frequency**: Constantly
- **When it applies**: All projects
- **Code references**: Fire Criteria Manual
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Standard 6-7 Fire Department Notes on General Notes sheet
  - Notes match current Fire Criteria Manual exactly
  - Includes timing of installations, hydrant installation, HS-20 loading, fire lane registration, vertical clearance
- **Common Failures**:
  - Notes missing or incomplete
  - Notes from outdated code version
  - Non-standard notes added
- **Detection/Evidence**: Compare notes to Fire Criteria Manual
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Add the 'Fire Department Notes' in the general notes section to quote the (7) standard & required notes exactly as indicated in the current City of Austin Fire Criteria Manual"
  - "Standard fire notes are out-of-date."

## 9. Special Hazards

### REQ-31: Dumpster Location
- **Frequency**: Frequently
- **When it applies**: All projects with dumpsters ≥ 1.5 cubic yards
- **Code references**: IFC 304.3.3
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Dumpsters not stored within buildings
  - Dumpsters not within 10 ft of combustible walls, openings, or roof eave lines
  - Exception: Areas protected by sprinkler system
  - Exception: Type I or IIA construction with exclusive dumpster storage
- **Common Failures**:
  - Dumpster within 10 ft of building openings
  - Dumpster location not shown
- **Detection/Evidence**: Locate dumpster on plans; measure to nearest building
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Dumpsters shall not be stored within buildings or within 10 ft of combustible walls, openings or roof eave lines. IFC 304.3.3"
  - "Please identify trash dumpster location and proximity to buildings."

### REQ-32: Fuel Storage Tanks
- **Frequency**: Sometimes
- **When it applies**: Projects with fuel storage
- **Code references**: IFC 5704.2.9.6.1.1, IFC 2303
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Tank location, fuel type, size, UL listing shown on plans
  - Aboveground tanks ≤660 gallons diesel: minimum 5 ft from property line and buildings
  - Propane tanks and diesel >500 gallons: risk assessment required
  - Vehicle fueling identified if applicable
  - Gas station specific: emergency shutoff 20-100 ft from dispensers, 6" concrete island or bollards
- **Common Failures**:
  - Tank location not shown
  - Setbacks not verified
  - Missing fuel type and size
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check for fuel storage; verify setbacks
- **Example Comments**:
  - "The location of all exterior tanks must be shown and the fuel labeled, tank size, standard of construction & method of containment indicated."
  - "Callout location of the Emergency shutoff, it shall be between 20 ft & 100 ft from dispensers- IFC 2303.2"

### REQ-33: Generators
- **Frequency**: Sometimes
- **When it applies**: Projects with generators
- **Code references**: IFC requirements
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Generator location shown
  - Fuel type specified
  - Tank volume/capacity indicated
  - UL listing provided
  - Data sheets submitted
- **Common Failures**:
  - Generator mentioned but not shown
  - Missing fuel/size information
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check for generator on plans
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Indicate what type of generator is proposed, the volume/capacity of the generator, provide data sheets and provide the UL listing."
  - "Provide details of the generator. Will it remain? Fuel type? Tank size?"

### REQ-34: High-Piled Storage
- **Frequency**: Sometimes
- **When it applies**: Buildings >12,000 SF that may contain storage >12 ft high
- **Code references**: IFC 3206.2, IFC 3206.6.1
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Building information provided to determine applicability
  - Commodity type and rack type verified
  - Sprinkler protection per IFC Table 3206.2
  - Access doors per IFC 3206.6.1
- **Common Failures**:
  - Building size triggers review but no info provided
  - Storage height not addressed
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check building size; request storage information
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Additional information is required to complete the review of this site. Provide the building height any building over 12,000 square feet that will allow high piled storage (storage over 12 ft high) will be required to meet IFC table 3206.2"
  - "Verify what commodities are present within the warehouse. Verify the type of racks being used and the height."

### REQ-35: Pipeline Setbacks
- **Frequency**: Rarely
- **When it applies**: Sites with major pipelines
- **Code references**: AFD requirement
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Pipeline location and easement shown
  - 0-50 ft: not addressed in comments (presumably not allowed)
  - 50-100 ft: minimum Type VA construction, 1-hour rated, non-combustible exterior, Class B/C roof
  - 100-200 ft: minimum Type VB construction, non-combustible exterior, Class B/C roof
  - Distance measured from pipeline centerline (or easement centerline if location unknown)
- **Common Failures**:
  - Pipeline not shown on plans
  - Required note not provided
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check for pipeline easements on plans
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Because there is major pipeline (20') running through a portion of this site and adjacent to it provide the following note... Construction within 50 to 100 feet of pipeline must be a minimum of VA construction type..."

### REQ-36: Building Separation
- **Frequency**: Sometimes
- **When it applies**: Multi-building sites, especially townhomes
- **Code references**: IRC R302.1, IBC
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Minimum 10 ft separation or 5 ft fire separation distance
  - <5 ft: 1-hour rated construction per IRC Table R302.1(1) or 13D sprinklers per R302.1(2)
  - Combined fire area when <5 ft separation
  - Only 2-hour fire walls create separate fire areas
- **Common Failures**:
  - Buildings too close without required ratings
  - Fire areas not combined when required
- **Detection/Evidence**: Measure building separations; check construction notes
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Please provide 10 separation minimum between building (pad 1 & 2.) Please note and dimension."
  - "Building separation from other buildings shall be a minimum 10 feet or fire separation distance of 5 feet."

## 10. Access Easements

### REQ-37: UDA/JUAE for Cross-Property Access
- **Frequency**: Frequently
- **When it applies**: Fire access or hydrant access across property lines
- **Code references**: AFD requirement
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Unified Development Agreement (UDA) or Joint Use Access Easement (JUAE) required
  - Recorded document copy provided for review
  - Boundaries shown on plans
  - Recording number called out on plans
  - Fire lane use clearly identified in document
- **Common Failures**:
  - No easement for cross-property access
  - Recorded document not provided
  - Recording number not on plans
  - Fire lane portion not visible in UDA
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check if fire access or hydrants cross property lines
- **Example Comments**:
  - "The access cannot be from an adjacent property unless there is either a Unified Development Agreement (UDA) or a Joint Use Access Easement (JUAE) between the two properties that legally binds this access together between the properties in perpetuity."
  - "Provide copies of the 'recorded' UDA or JUAE for review by AFD and clearly show their boundaries on the plans and callout the associated Travis County document record number on the plans."

## 11. Riser Rooms and Knox Boxes

### REQ-38: Fire Riser Room Location
- **Frequency**: Frequently
- **When it applies**: All sprinkled buildings
- **Code references**: NFPA 13, AFD requirement
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Riser room location shown on plans
  - Fire line route matches riser room location
  - Exterior door preferred (eliminates PIV requirement)
  - Knox box at exterior door
- **Common Failures**:
  - Riser room location not shown
  - Fire line doesn't reach riser room location
  - Two different locations shown
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check utility and site plans for riser room callout
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Show fire riser room location on the utility sheet."
  - "Fire riser room (plan west) on the office building does not match the location where the fire line enters the building (plan east)."
  - "There are two different fire riser room locations. Clarify where the exact fire riser room location is."

### REQ-39: Knox Box Requirements
- **Frequency**: Frequently
- **When it applies**: All commercial buildings, gated properties
- **Code references**: IFC 506.1
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Knox box at main entrance
  - Knox box at riser room exterior door
  - Knox box at mechanical rooms and fire control rooms
  - Knox box on ingress side of gates
  - Contains keys for: main doors, mechanical rooms, fire control room, elevators, other secured areas
- **Common Failures**:
  - Knox box not shown
  - Knox box on wrong side of gate
  - Knox box location away from riser room
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check for Knox box callouts at appropriate locations
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Relocate Knox Box to the wall outside the fire riser room. It is currently shown on a wall away from the riser room location. IFC 506.1"
  - "Man gate blocking access will need knox lock or key provided in knox box located at the front door."

## 12. Phasing

### REQ-40: Phasing Plan Requirements
- **Frequency**: Sometimes
- **When it applies**: Phased development projects
- **Code references**: IFC 106.2.4.1, IBC 107.3.3
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Phase boundaries clearly identified with phasing line type
  - Each phase numbered/labeled
  - Fire lanes and hydrants completed in Phase 1
  - Temporary turnarounds where fire lanes extend into future phases
  - Phasing notes for occupied phases addressing:
    - Approved exiting to public way
    - Fire department access roads completed
    - Private hydrants completed
    - FDCs maintained
    - Sprinkler/fire alarm shop drawings include phasing
    - No dead-end corridors >20 ft (50 ft with 13 sprinklers)
- **Common Failures**:
  - Phase boundaries not shown
  - Fire lane extends into unapproved phase without turnaround
  - Phasing notes incomplete
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check for phasing plan sheet; verify phase boundaries
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Revise the Phasing plan to indicate the Building Number associated with each phase."
  - "Add note on master site and utility sheet that states all fire lanes and hydrants shall be installed in phase 1."
  - "Fire lanes for this property exceeds 150 feet and will be required to have at least a temporary turn around where it crosses into lot 4 and 5."

## 13. Miscellaneous

### REQ-41: Plan Scale Accuracy
- **Frequency**: Sometimes
- **When it applies**: All plans
- **Code references**: AFD requirement
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - Plans are to scale
  - Dimensions match when scaled
- **Common Failures**:
  - Scale incorrect
  - PDF scaling issues
- **Detection/Evidence**: Verify dimensions by scaling
- **Example Comments**:
  - "The scale on the site plan sheets appear to be incorrect."
  - "The dimensional control plan is not to scale – revise."

### REQ-42: Construction Document Status
- **Frequency**: Sometimes
- **When it applies**: Final approval stage
- **Code references**: AFD requirement
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - "Not for Construction" notes removed before approval
  - "Bid Set" or "Bid Documents" notes removed
  - Plans signed and sealed by EOR
- **Common Failures**:
  - Preliminary notes remaining on plans
  - Missing seals/signatures
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check for construction status notes
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Remove all references to 'Bid Documents' or 'Bid Set'. AFD will not approve any plan sets that are not for construction purposes."
  - "Text at bottom of all pages indicating that this 'For regulatory review only – Not For Construction' must be removed prior to site plan approval."

### REQ-43: Obstructions and Clear Access
- **Frequency**: Sometimes
- **When it applies**: Site plan review
- **Code references**: Various IFC sections
- **Pass Criteria**:
  - No obstructions in fire lanes (call boxes, bollards, etc.)
  - Clear path around buildings for firefighter access (minimum 5 ft stable surface)
  - Fences with man gates and Knox boxes where access required
  - Breezeways 2-hour rated with sprinklers for hose lay routes
- **Common Failures**:
  - Call box in fire lane island
  - Fence without gate for rear access
  - Unrated breezeway used for hose lay distance
- **Detection/Evidence**: Check for obstructions in fire lanes; verify clear paths
- **Example Comments**:
  - "There appears to be a call box in the island at the entrance that obstructs the fire lane."
  - "Breezeway between Buildings 4B & 5, as well as the breezeway between Buildings 5 & 6 need to be 2 hr. rated with fire sprinkler coverage provided in order for hoselay to be allowed through this passage."
  - "AFD requires a minimum clear access width of 5ft on a stable and reasonably level walking surface to accommodate responding firefighters"

  "content": "# FIRE Department Procedures and Coordination

## Multi-Step Procedural Workflows

### PROC-01: Fire Flow Determination and Verification
**When applies**: All projects
**Purpose**: Establish required fire flow and verify available water supply
**Steps**:
1. **Calculate Fire Flow Demand**
   - Determine worst-case (most demanding) building
   - Calculate fire area (all floors + horizontal roof projections)
   - Apply IFC Table B105.1(2) for commercial or B105.1(1) for residential
   - Use correct construction classification (not occupancy)
2. **Apply Sprinkler Reductions**
   - NFPA 13: up to 75% reduction, minimum 1000 gpm
   - NFPA 13R: up to 50% reduction, minimum 1500 gpm
   - Type V construction: maximum 50% regardless of system
3. **Obtain AFD Flow Test**
   - Request test from AFD (not third-party)
   - Test location near point of connection
   - Both pages required
   - Must be within 1 year of submittal
4. **Verify Available Fire Flow**
   - Calculate available flow at 20 psi from test data
   - Available must meet or exceed required demand
   - Maximum 10 fps velocity in mains
5. **Document on Cover Sheet**
   - Complete AFD Information Table
   - Show fire flow before deductions
   - Show reduced fire flow
   - Include test date and location
**Completion Criteria**: Cover sheet table complete, flow test in plan set, available flow meets demand
**Common Sticking Points**:
- Wrong fire area (not including all floors)
- Claiming 75% reduction for combustible construction
- Expired flow test
- Wrong IFC year in table
**Code References**: IFC 507.1, IFC Appendix B, Fire Criteria Manual

### PROC-02: Private Hydrant System Design
**When applies**: Projects with private fire hydrants
**Purpose**: Verify private hydrant system can deliver required fire flow
**Steps**:
1. **Identify Private Hydrants**
   - Distinguish from public hydrants (on private property or private main)
   - Label as "Private" in callouts
2. **Prepare Hydraulic Calculations**
   - Sealed by TX Licensed Professional Engineer
   - Use correct C-factors (110 PVC, 80 DI)
   - Show all nodes, pipe sizes, fittings, valves
   - Include network schematic
3. **Calculate Fire Flow Delivery**
   - Flow all required hydrants simultaneously
   - Most remote hydrant: 1250 gpm max
   - Additional hydrants: remainder of demand
   - Maintain 20 psi residual minimum
   - Velocity ≤10 fps in mains (allowed to exceed in 6" lead)
4. **Include on Utility Plan**
   - NFPA 24 installation note
   - "All private hydrants shall be painted red" note
**Completion Criteria**: Sealed calculations in plan set, notes on utility plan, hydrants labeled Private
**Common Sticking Points**:
- Calculations not sealed
- Wrong C-factors used
- Missing variables in calculation
- Velocity exceeds limits
**Code References**: NFPA 24, Fire Criteria Manual

### PROC-03: Alternative Surface Fire Lane Approval
**When applies**: Grass-pave, geoblock, paver, pervious fire lanes
**Purpose**: Verify alternative surface can support fire apparatus
**Steps**:
1. **Engage Geotechnical Engineer**
   - TX Licensed Geotechnical PE required
   - Site-specific soil analysis
   - Subgrade preparation requirements
2. **Develop Section Design**
   - Sealed by Geotech PE
   - State meets HS-20 loading (32,000 lb/axle, 80,000 lb gross)
   - For aerial operations (25 ft lane): 43,200 lbs on 24"x24" outrigger
   - Include all layers, depths, materials
3. **Address Drainage**
   - Minimum 2% slope for vegetated surfaces
   - 1% for asphalt, 0.5% for concrete
   - French drains if recommended
   - No concentrated runoff on vegetated surfaces
4. **Include Design Elements**
   - 6-inch ribbon curb to contain materials
   - Nonwoven filter fabric encapsulating flex base
   - Fire lane signage and edge marking
5. **Provide Manufacturer Data**
   - Data sheets for grass-pave, geoblock, etc.
   - Include make and model in callouts
6. **Match Adjacent Surface Transitions**
   - "Bridged" design across surface transitions
   - More stringent design extends 2 ft under adjacent surface
**Completion Criteria**: Sealed geotech report in plan set, section detail with HS-20 statement, drainage design, manufacturer data
**Common Sticking Points**:
- Details without sealed geotech report
- Grading conflicts between geotech report and plans
- Missing ribbon curb
- Drainage slopes below minimum
**Code References**: IFC 503.2.3, Fire Criteria Manual

### PROC-04: AWU Coordination and Final Sign-off
**When applies**: All projects
**Purpose**: Coordinate fire flow impacts with Austin Water Utility
**Steps**:
1. **AWU Evaluates Water System Impacts**
   - Fire flow demand provided to AWU
   - AWU verifies system can deliver flow without excessive velocity
   - Maximum 10 fps in public mains
   - System Extension Request (SER) may be required
2. **Resolve AWU Comments**
   - Address any pipe sizing issues
   - Verify fire line connections
   - Confirm hydrant lead sizing
3. **Obtain AWU Approval**
   - AWU signs off on plans
4. **Schedule AFD Final Sign-off**
   - Contact AFD reviewer for appointment
   - Obtain electronic or mylar signatures
**Completion Criteria**: AWU signature obtained, AFD sign-off scheduled, final signatures applied
**Common Sticking Points**:
- AWU requires larger tap or main extension
- Fire flow demand provided to AWU doesn't match plans
- Static pressure discrepancies
- SER required but not anticipated
**Code References**: Fire Criteria Manual

### PROC-05: AMOC (Alternative Method of Compliance) Process
**When applies**: Projects requiring code deviations
**Purpose**: Document and approve alternative approaches
**Steps**:
1. **Identify Need for AMOC**
   - Fire access cannot be met
   - Street width insufficient
   - Hydrant spacing cannot be met
   - Other code deviation required
2. **Submit AMOC Separately**
   - AMOC submitted outside site plan process
   - Submit to AFD reviewer
   - Include justification and alternative measures
3. **Obtain AMOC Approval**
   - AFD reviews and approves
   - AMOC number and date issued
4. **Include in Site Plan**
   - Reference AMOC on cover sheet table
   - Include approved AMOC in plan set with next update
   - Update fire flow table if AMOC affects requirements
**Completion Criteria**: AMOC approved separately, referenced on cover sheet, copy in plan set
**Common Sticking Points**:
- AMOC submitted with site plan instead of separately
- Cover sheet not updated to reflect AMOC
- AMOC affects fire flow but table not revised
**Code References**: AFD requirement

### PROC-06: Phased Occupancy Fire Protection
**When applies**: Phased development with partial occupancy
**Purpose**: Ensure fire protection during phased construction
**Steps**:
1. **Develop Phasing Plan**
   - Phase boundaries clearly shown
   - Building numbers associated with phases
   - Phasing line type defined
2. **Phase 1 Requirements**
   - All fire lanes and hydrants completed
   - Temporary turnarounds where lanes extend to future phases
3. **Occupied Phase Requirements**
   - Required exiting to public way approved
   - No dead-end corridors >20 ft (50 ft with NFPA 13)
   - Fire department access roads completed
   - Private hydrants completed
   - FDCs maintained visible and accessible
   - Exterior building envelope approved
   - No exposed framing
   - Signage at doors to incomplete phases
4. **Documentation**
   - Phasing notes in plan set
   - Sprinkler and fire alarm shop drawings include phasing
**Completion Criteria**: Phasing plan complete, Phase 1 fire protection in place, occupied phase meets all requirements
**Common Sticking Points**:
- Phase boundaries not clearly shown
- Fire lane extends into future phase without turnaround
- Phasing notes incomplete
**Code References**: IFC 106.2.4.1, IBC 107.3.3

## Detailed Cross-Department Coordination

### Austin Water Utility (AWU)
**When Required**: All projects with water connections
**What They Provide**:
- Water system capacity analysis
- Fire flow impact evaluation
- System Extension Request (SER) determination
- Water main velocity verification
- Tap and connection approval
**Sequencing**:
1. AFD reviews fire flow demand and hydrant layout
2. AWU evaluates system impacts
3. AWU provides comments/approval
4. AFD final sign-off after AWU approval
**Common Issues**:
- Fire flow demand discrepancy between AFD table and AWU table
- Available fire flow calculated differently
- Tap size insufficient for fire flow
- SER required for system improvements
- Static pressure discrepancy between flow test and AWU records
**Example Comments**:
- "Impacts to the Austin Water Utility (AWU) piping system due to providing the required fire flow for a development project are evaluated by and resolved through the staff of AWU."
- "Contact me to schedule my signoff on the final mylar plan set once you have obtained approval signatures from the AWU."
- "SER on page 4 indicates that AWU engineering was provided a fire flow of 1500 GPM to determine the need for a SER but the actual required fire flow is 2125 GPM"

### Austin Transportation Department (ATD)
**When Required**: Street width issues, parking restriction requests
**What They Provide**:
- Approval of restricted parking for fire access
- Street operational width confirmation
- Traffic control coordination
**Sequencing**:
1. AFD identifies street width deficiency
2. Design team requests parking restriction or AMOC
3. ATD reviews and approves parking restrictions
4. AMOC documented with ATD approval
**Common Issues**:
- Street not wide enough for 25 ft fire lane with parking
- No Parking signs required on one or both sides
- Bike lane conflicts with fire access needs
**Example Comments**:
- "Seton Avenue and West 26th Street widths do not provide sufficient operational area for an AFD apparatus for the proposed development. Either provide a plan to increase the street width (include in demo package) or restrict the parking on at least one curb line. Restricted parking shall be documented in an alternate method of compliance with ATD approvals"

### Land Use Review (Structural)
**When Required**: Underground structures beneath fire lanes
**What They Provide**:
- Structural review of underground facilities
- HB-17 loading verification for elevated roadways
- Detention pond lid capacity verification
**Sequencing**:
1. AFD identifies fire lane over underground structure
2. Structural engineer provides calculations
3. Land Use Review (structural) reviews calculations
4. AFD approves based on structural confirmation
**Common Issues**:
- Detention pond under fire lane creates collapse risk
- Structural calculations incomplete
- Missing reinforcement details
- Design assumptions not documented
**Example Comments**:
- "The structural pond drawing is currently lacking information, such as dimensions, details similar to the retaining wall sections shown shall be provided for the pond wall sections"
- "Please update the general notes to indicate the detention pond live load considered in the design of the detention pond lid as required by the IFC and local amendments"

### Commercial Plan Review (Building)
**When Required**: All commercial projects
**What They Provide**:
- Building construction type verification
- Occupancy classification
- Sprinkler system type confirmation
- Building height verification
**Sequencing**:
- Site plan and building permit reviews may overlap
- Sprinkler system type must match between reviews
- Construction type must be consistent
**Common Issues**:
- Site plan sprinkler type doesn't match building permit
- Construction classification on site plan doesn't match building plans
- Building height not verified on site plans
**Example Comments**:
- "FYI the sprinkler system type shown on the site plan has to match the sprinkler system type indicated in the project building permit review plans otherwise the building plans will be rejected until it does."
- "Verify with owner that they will be using a Full NFPA 13 System and not an NFPA 13R (which is what usually applies to this type of R-2 occupancy)"

## External Agency Coordination

### Travis County ESD
**Type**: Fire jurisdiction authority
**When Required**: Projects in Limited Purpose Jurisdiction (LPJ)
**What They Provide**:
- Fire code review for county jurisdiction
- Independent approval required
**Timing**: Concurrent with AFD review
**Common Issues**:
- Conflicting requirements between City and County
- Design team unaware of dual jurisdiction
- Different code editions may apply
**Example Comments**:
- "This project is located in the Austin Limited Purpose Jurisdiction, because of this, both the City of Austin and Travis County have permitting jurisdiction over the project for fire related items. Therefore, the project shall comply with both the City of Austin Fire Department requirements and Travis County ESD## requirements."

### TDLR (Texas Dept. of Licensing and Regulation)
**Type**: State accessibility authority
**When Required**: Phased occupancy with accessible elements
**What They Provide**:
- Elevator approval
- Accessible route approval
**Timing**: Before phased occupancy
**Common Issues**:
- Elevator serving occupied phase not TDLR approved
- Accessible means of egress not approved
**Example Comments**:
- "If required for accessible means of egress, the elevator serving the phase shall be approved by TDLR and the City of Austin."

### Pipeline Operators
**Type**: Utility coordination
**When Required**: Major pipelines crossing or adjacent to site
**What They Provide**:
- Pipeline location confirmation
- Coordination on construction near pipeline
**Timing**: During design phase
**Common Issues**:
- Pipeline not shown on plans
- Construction type doesn't meet setback requirements
**Example Comments**:
- "See the Northeast corner of the site plan where it calls out a 20' gasoline pipeline across a portion of the property lines of this project."

## Common Process Breakdowns

| Issue | How to Detect | Impact | Correct Approach | Frequency |
|-------|---------------|--------|------------------|-----------|
| Fire flow table before/after reductions confusion | Cover sheet shows reduced fire flow in "Fire Flow Demand" field | Incorrect fire flow documented, potential hydrant spacing errors | "Fire Flow Demand" = before reductions; "Reduced Fire Flow" = after | High |
| AWU and AFD fire flow discrepancy | AWU table available fire flow doesn't match AFD calculation | Conflicting information in plan set | Verify calculation method; use AFD formula at 20 psi | Medium |
| Flow test location mismatch | Flow test from hydrant far from project tie-in | May not represent actual water supply conditions | Request flow test at or near tie-in point | Medium |
| Expired flow test | Flow test date >1 year from submittal | Invalid water supply documentation | Request new AFD flow test | High |
| Site plan/building permit sprinkler mismatch | Site plan shows 13R, building permit shows 13 | Building permit rejection, fire flow recalculation | Verify sprinkler type early; coordinate between reviews | Medium |
| Construction type/occupancy confusion | "B" shown for construction classification | Occupancy vs construction confusion | Construction classification = IBC Type (IA, IB, IIA, etc.) | High |
| AMOC submitted with site plan | AMOC document included in site plan update | AMOC not processed, delays approval | Submit AMOC separately; include approved copy in plan set | Medium |
| Missing recorded easement | UDA/JUAE mentioned but not provided | Cannot verify cross-property access rights | Request recorded document with recording number | Medium |
| Underground structure under fire lane | Fire lane routes over detention pond | Risk of collapse during emergency; AFD may reject | Relocate fire lane or facility; or provide structural proof | Low |
| Informal Update status misunderstanding | Project approved as "Informal Update" | Design team assumes approval | Informal Update ≠ final approval; formal approval still required | Medium |

| Document | When Required | Must Contain | Common Issues | Code Reference |

| AFD Fire Hydrant Flow Test Report | All projects | Both pages of test, date, location, static pressure, residual pressure, flow rate | Expired (>1 year old), only one page submitted, location far from tie-in point, third-party test instead of AFD | IFC 507.4 (Local), Fire Criteria Manual Appendix E |
| Cover Sheet AFD Information Table | All projects | Fire codes, fire flow demand, intended use, construction classification, fire area, sprinkler type, reduced fire flow, test date/location, high-rise status, AMOC | Wrong IFC year, occupancy vs construction classification confusion, fire flow after reductions instead of before, missing fields | AFD requirement |
| Private Hydrant Hydraulic Calculations | Projects with private fire hydrants | Sealed by TX PE, pipe sizes, fittings, valves, nodes, network schematic, residual pressures, velocities, C-factors (110 PVC, 80 DI) | Missing calculations, not sealed, wrong C-factors, incomplete variables, velocity >10 fps | Fire Criteria Manual, NFPA 24 |
| Geotechnical Report (Alternative Surface Fire Lane) | Grass-pave, geoblock, paver fire lanes | Signed/sealed by TX Geotechnical PE, section design, HS-20 loading statement, drainage design, soil analysis, subgrade preparation | Missing report, details only without geotech letter, grading conflicts with report, missing French drain recommendations | IFC 503.2.3, Fire Criteria Manual |
| Fire Lane Marking/Signage Detail | All projects with fire lanes | COA Standard Detail 901S-6, fire lane striping detail, sign locations | Missing detail, wrong wording ("No Parking" vs "FIRE ZONE/TOW-AWAY ZONE"), sign height not specified | IFC 503.3.2 (Local) |
| UDA or JUAE (recorded) | Fire access or hydrants crossing property lines | Recording number, fire lane designation in document, easement boundaries | Document not recorded, fire lane use not specified, boundaries not shown on plans, recording number not called out | AFD requirement |
| Pavement Section Detail | Fire lanes, especially alternative surfaces | HS-20 loading statement, reinforcement (ACI standards), subgrade preparation, material specifications | No load rating shown, H20 instead of HS-20, missing reinforcement details | IFC 503.2.6 |
| AMOC (Alternative Method of Compliance) | Projects requiring code deviations | Approved AMOC number, approval date, description of alternative | AMOC referenced but not approved, AMOC submitted with site plan instead of separately | AFD requirement |
| Sprinkler Designer Letter | Fire line <6" for NFPA 13 system | TX Licensed RME signature, sprinkler type, justification for smaller line | 4" line shown without justification | NFPA 13 |
| Facility Closure Plan | Existing hazmat facilities being demolished/redeveloped | Disposal/transport plan for hazardous materials, new location address | Not submitted when hazmat permit exists | IFC 5001.6.3 |
| Building Elevations | Buildings near property lines, opening verification | All sides, story heights, opening locations and percentages | Not provided when needed to verify fire separation | IBC/IRC R302.1 |

## Conditional Triggers

### TRG-01: Sprinkled Building
- **IF**: Building has automatic fire sprinkler system
- **THEN**:
  - Fire access distance increases to 200 ft (from 150 ft)
  - Hydrant distance increases to 500 ft for primary (from 400 ft)
  - Fire flow reduction allowed per system type
  - Sprinkler type must be specified on cover sheet
  - Fire line notes required on utility plan
  - PIV or riser room exterior door required (NFPA 13)
  - FDC required
- **Detection Method**: Check cover sheet for sprinkler system type; look for fire line on utility plans
- **Evidence to Look For**: AFD table sprinkler field, fire line callouts, FDC location
- **Frequency**: High
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-01 (modified), REQ-08 (modified), REQ-14, REQ-17-22, REQ-23
- **Related Documents**: None additional
- **Example Comments**:
  - "For sprinkled buildings, this distance may increase to 200ft. IFC 503.1.1"
  - "EXCEPTION: For sprinklered buildings (13 or 13R) the first hydrant can be 500 ft"

### TRG-02: Fire Flow ≥ 1500 GPM
- **IF**: Required fire flow is 1500 gpm or more
- **THEN**:
  - Second fire hydrant required within 500 ft of all exterior wall points
  - Hydrant across divided highway not acceptable as secondary
- **Detection Method**: Calculate fire flow from building area and construction type
- **Evidence to Look For**: Fire area, construction type, fire flow on cover sheet
- **Frequency**: High
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-09
- **Related Documents**: None
- **Example Comments**:
  - "A second hydrant is required within 500 ft if the fire flow is 1500 gpm or more. IFC 507.5.1"

### TRG-03: Private Fire Hydrants
- **IF**: Site has private fire hydrants (on private property or private fire main)
- **THEN**:
  - Hydraulic calculations required (sealed by TX PE)
  - NFPA 24 note required on utility plan
  - "All private hydrants shall be painted red" note required
  - Private hydrants must be clearly identified in callouts
- **Detection Method**: Check if hydrants are on private property or connected to private fire main
- **Evidence to Look For**: Hydrant locations vs property lines, PUE callouts, private fire main
- **Frequency**: High
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-11, REQ-16, REQ-20
- **Related Documents**: Private Hydrant Hydraulic Calculations
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Utility Plan – there are private fire hydrants on the site, clearly call them out as Private"
  - "For private hydrants the engineer shall provide sealed calculations"

### TRG-04: High-Rise Building
- **IF**: Highest story floor level > 30 ft above lowest fire department vehicle access
- **THEN**:
  - Standpipe system required
  - Dual FDCs required on adjacent walls
  - FDCs within 100 ft of hydrant (may extend to 300 ft with signage)
  - Class III standpipe connections
- **Detection Method**: Check building height callouts or floor elevations
- **Evidence to Look For**: Building height on cover sheet, number of stories, floor elevations
- **Frequency**: Medium
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-25, REQ-26
- **Related Documents**: None
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Standpipe systems shall be installed throughout buildings where the floor level of the highest story is located more than 30 feet above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access. IFC 905.3.1"
  - "For High Rise building a minimum of (2) remote FDCs are required for the standpipe system per NFPA 14, Section 7.12.2"

### TRG-05: NFPA 13 Sprinkler System
- **IF**: Building requires or proposes full NFPA 13 sprinkler system
- **THEN**:
  - Minimum 6" fire line (or calculations for smaller)
  - NFPA 13 installation note required on utility plan
  - PIV required (or wall PIV, or exterior riser room door)
  - Up to 75% fire flow reduction (minimum 1000 gpm for non-combustible)
  - Fire line installation by licensed sprinkler contractor
- **Detection Method**: Check cover sheet sprinkler type; occupancy requires NFPA 13
- **Evidence to Look For**: Non-residential occupancy, building exceeding 13R limits, cover sheet
- **Frequency**: High
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-17, REQ-18, REQ-19, REQ-21
- **Related Documents**: Sprinkler Designer Letter (if <6" line)
- **Example Comments**:
  - "For full 13 installations the underground fire line must be a minimum of 6 inch unless calculations or other justification is provided"
  - "For full 13 installations a post indicator valve must be provided in the underground fire line lead-in"

### TRG-06: Gates Across Fire Lanes
- **IF**: Site has gates (manual or motorized) across fire access roads
- **THEN**:
  - Gate type must be identified (manual vs motorized)
  - Gate width must match fire lane width
  - Knox key switch for motorized gates
  - Knox box for manual gates
  - UL 325 listed operators for power gates
  - ASTM F2200 compliant design
  - Manual override for power loss
  - Standard gate notes required on site plan
- **Detection Method**: Look for gates on site plan
- **Evidence to Look For**: Gate symbols, callouts, Knox device callouts
- **Frequency**: Medium
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-27
- **Related Documents**: None
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Gates across fire access roads must have the appropriate width and electric gates must be provided with a Knox key switch. IFC 503.6"
  - "Please note if gate is manual or power operated"

### TRG-07: Dead-End Fire Lane > 150 ft
- **IF**: Fire lane dead end exceeds 150 ft
- **THEN**:
  - Approved turnaround required
  - Turnaround must match Fire Criteria Manual Appendix G
- **Detection Method**: Measure dead-end fire lane lengths
- **Evidence to Look For**: Fire lane configuration, turnaround locations
- **Frequency**: High
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-04
- **Related Documents**: None
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Fire Department access roads may not have dead ends longer that 150 ft without provisions for approved turnaround. IFC 503.2.5"

### TRG-08: Alternative Surface Fire Lane
- **IF**: Fire lane surface is grass-pave, geoblock, pavers, pervious pavement, or other non-asphalt/concrete
- **THEN**:
  - Geotechnical report required (sealed by TX Geotech PE)
  - Section detail stating HS-20 loading
  - Minimum 2% slope for vegetated surfaces
  - 6" ribbon curb required
  - Filter fabric encapsulating flex base
  - Fire lane signage and edge marking
  - For aerial operations: support 43,200 lbs on 24"x24" outrigger
  - Manufacturer data sheets required
- **Detection Method**: Look for alternative surface materials in legend or callouts
- **Evidence to Look For**: Grass-pave, geoblock, paver, pervious pavement symbols/callouts
- **Frequency**: Medium
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-06
- **Related Documents**: Geotechnical Report, Manufacturer Data Sheets
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Other surfaces may be approved based on submittal of engineering documentation proving they can withstand the HS-20 loading"
  - "Provide a signed and sealed geotechnical report for the Geoblock fire lanes"

### TRG-09: Fire Access Across Property Lines
- **IF**: Fire department access or hydrant access crosses property lines
- **THEN**:
  - UDA or JUAE required
  - Recorded document must be provided
  - Document must specify fire lane use
  - Boundaries shown on plans
  - Recording number called out on plans
- **Detection Method**: Check if fire lanes or hydrant access routes cross property boundaries
- **Evidence to Look For**: Property lines, fire lane routing, hydrant locations
- **Frequency**: Medium
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-37
- **Related Documents**: UDA or JUAE (recorded)
- **Example Comments**:
  - "The access cannot be from an adjacent property unless there is either a Unified Development Agreement (UDA) or a Joint Use Access Easement (JUAE)"

### TRG-10: Phased Development
- **IF**: Project is developed in multiple phases
- **THEN**:
  - Phasing plan required with phase boundaries
  - Fire lanes and hydrants in Phase 1
  - Temporary turnarounds where fire lanes extend to future phases
  - Phasing notes for each phase
  - Sprinkler and fire alarm shop drawings include phasing
- **Detection Method**: Check for phasing in project description or phasing plans
- **Evidence to Look For**: Phasing notes, phase boundaries, phase numbering
- **Frequency**: Medium
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-40
- **Related Documents**: Phasing Plan
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Add note on master site and utility sheet that states all fire lanes and hydrants shall be installed in phase 1"
  - "Fire lanes for this property exceeds 150 feet and will be required to have at least a temporary turn around where it crosses into lot 4 and 5"

### TRG-11: Hazardous Materials On-Site
- **IF**: Site has existing hazmat permits, fuel storage >500 gal, or hazardous operations
- **THEN**:
  - Chemical inventory required
  - Tank locations, types, sizes shown
  - Risk assessment may be required
  - Facility Closure Plan for demolition
  - Special setback requirements
- **Detection Method**: Check for fuel tanks, chemical storage, industrial operations
- **Evidence to Look For**: Tank symbols, hazmat permits, industrial occupancy
- **Frequency**: Low
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-32, REQ-33
- **Related Documents**: Facility Closure Plan, Chemical Inventory, Risk Assessment
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Provide a complete inventory of chemicals inside and outside to be used and stored on site"
  - "Provide AFD with a Facility Closure Plan in accordance with 2021 International Fire Code Section 5001.6.3"

### TRG-12: Gas Station/Fuel Dispensing
- **IF**: Site includes vehicle fueling operations
- **THEN**:
  - Emergency shutoff 20-100 ft from dispensers
  - Dispensers on 6" concrete island or protected by bollards
  - Fuel type, tank size, UL listing required
- **Detection Method**: Look for fuel dispensing equipment on plans
- **Evidence to Look For**: Fuel pump symbols, canopy over dispensers, tank locations
- **Frequency**: Low
- **Activated Requirements**: REQ-32
- **Related Documents**: None
- **Example Comments**:
  - "Callout location of the Emergency shutoff, it shall be between 20 ft & 100 ft from dispensers- IFC 2303.2"
  - "Dispensers must be on a 6 in concrete island – IFC 2306.7.3 or protected by bollards"

### TRG-13: Limited Purpose Jurisdiction (LPJ)
- **IF**: Project is in City of Austin Limited Purpose Jurisdiction
- **THEN**:
  - Both City of Austin AFD and Travis County ESD have jurisdiction
  - Use most stringent requirement from either AHJ
  - Coordinate with both reviewing authorities
- **Detection Method**: Check project location/jurisdiction notes
- **Evidence to Look For**: LPJ designation, ETJ references, Travis County ESD mentions
- **Frequency**: Low

# Fire (AFD) — Discipline Finding

**Property:** 9101 Cameron Rd, Austin, TX 78753
**Zoning:** CS (General Commercial Services)
**Lot Area:** 1.01 AC / 44,150 SF
**Proposed:** AutoZone retail store, 7,375 SF single-story (Prototype 74)
**Occupancy:** Group M (Mercantile) — IBC
**Construction Type:** Not specified on concept plan (shown as "XX"); assumed Type V-B for worst-case fire flow analysis
**Discipline:** Austin Fire Department (AFD) — fire access, hydrants, sprinklers, fire flow, FDC
**Risk Level:** LOW-TO-MODERATE — standard single-story commercial retail; no high-rise, no standpipe, no unusual hazards; primary risks are fire lane geometry on a tight site and hydrant coverage verification

---

## 1. Building Classification and Sprinkler Determination

### Occupancy and Construction Type

The proposed AutoZone is a single-story retail store selling auto parts. Under the IBC this is **Group M (Mercantile)** occupancy. The concept plan does not specify the construction type (labeled "XX"), but typical single-story AutoZone prototype buildings use **Type V-B (unprotected combustible frame)** or **Type II-B (unprotected non-combustible steel)**. The fire flow analysis below uses the worst-case assumption of Type V-B; if the building is ultimately Type II-B, fire flow demand will be lower.

### Sprinkler Requirement

Under the 2021 IFC as locally amended by the City of Austin, an automatic sprinkler system is required for Group M occupancies exceeding **12,000 SF** (IFC 903.2.7). At 7,375 SF, this building is **below the IFC area threshold** for a mandatory sprinkler system based solely on occupancy area.

However, several factors may still trigger or motivate a sprinkler installation:

1. **AutoZone corporate standard:** AutoZone prototype stores typically include NFPA 13 sprinkler systems as a corporate design standard regardless of code mandates.
2. **IFC 903.2.7 Exception 1:** The building must also be evaluated for high-piled storage provisions (IFC Chapter 32) if storage exceeds 12 ft in height within any portion of the building. AutoZone stores routinely store inventory on racks above 12 ft, which would trigger **IFC 3206.2** sprinkler requirements for high-piled combustible storage regardless of building area.
3. **Fire flow and hydrant benefits:** A sprinklered building earns relaxed fire access distance (200 ft vs. 150 ft) and hydrant distance (500 ft vs. 400 ft), both of which are advantageous on this constrained site.

**Assessment:** An **NFPA 13 sprinkler system** should be assumed for this project. If the building is sprinklered, it will be NFPA 13 (not 13R or 13D) because this is a commercial M-occupancy building. This triggers TRG-01 and TRG-05 in the AFD review framework.

### High-Rise and Standpipe

- **High-rise (IFC 403):** Not applicable. The building is single-story, approximately 20 ft tall, well below the 75-ft high-rise threshold.
- **Standpipe (IFC 905.3.1):** Not required. The highest floor is not more than 30 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access.

---

## 2. Fire Flow Analysis

### Fire Flow Demand Calculation

Per IFC Appendix B, Table B105.1(2) for commercial buildings:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Building fire area | 7,375 SF (single story, no horizontal roof projection overhang specified) |
| Construction type (worst-case) | Type V-B |
| Fire flow demand per Table B105.1(2) | **1,500 gpm at 20 psi residual** |

For a Type V-B building with fire area of 7,375 SF, Table B105.1(2) yields a required fire flow of 1,500 gpm. If construction is Type II-B (non-combustible), the fire flow would drop to approximately 1,500 gpm as well (the table floor for this area range is 1,500 gpm regardless of type at this building size).

### Sprinkler Reduction

Assuming an NFPA 13 sprinkler system is installed:

| Construction Type | Maximum Reduction | Minimum After Reduction | Reduced Fire Flow |
|---|---|---|---|
| Type V-B (combustible) | 50% per IFC Table B105.2 | 750 gpm, but 1,000 gpm minimum per table | **1,000 gpm** |
| Type II-B (non-combustible) | 75% per IFC Table B105.2 | 1,000 gpm minimum | **1,000 gpm** |

**Key note on combustible construction:** If the building is Type V (combustible), the maximum fire flow reduction is **50%**, not 75%. This is a frequent AFD comment (REQ-14, TRG-16). The reduced fire flow lands at 1,000 gpm minimum regardless of construction type for this building.

### Hydrant Count Threshold

At a reduced fire flow of **1,000 gpm** (below the 1,500 gpm threshold), only **one** fire hydrant is required within the applicable distance. A second hydrant is not required by code. TRG-02 (fire flow >= 1,500 gpm requiring a second hydrant) does **not** trigger if the sprinkler system is installed and the reduction is taken.

If the building is **not** sprinklered, the full 1,500 gpm demand applies and a **second hydrant within 500 ft** would be required per IFC 507.5.1.

### Available Fire Flow

The concept plan does not include an AFD fire hydrant flow test. An AFD-conducted flow test (not third-party) must be obtained within 1 year of site plan submittal, tested at or near the point of connection. Both pages of the test report must be submitted (REQ-12).

The site is served by an existing **36-inch water main** and an existing **14-inch water main** along Cameron Road, plus an existing 8-inch line. A 36-inch trunk main is likely to provide ample available fire flow (well above 1,500 gpm at 20 psi residual). **Available fire flow is not expected to be a constraint**, but formal verification via the AFD flow test is mandatory.

**Citation:** IFC 507.4 (Local Amendment), Fire Criteria Manual Appendix E.

---

## 3. Fire Department Access Roads (Fire Lanes)

### Fire Access Distance Requirement

| Condition | Maximum Hose Lay Distance | Code Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Non-sprinklered building | 150 ft from fire lane to all exterior wall points | IFC 503.1.1 |
| Sprinklered building (NFPA 13) | 200 ft from fire lane to all exterior wall points | IFC 503.1.1 |

Distance is measured as **hose lay at ground level around obstructions** -- it cannot be measured through or under the building (REQ-01).

### Fire Lane Layout Assessment (from Concept Plan)

The concept plan (Sheet 01) shows a "Proposed Fire Lane" line type in the legend, and the plan depicts fire lane routing on the site. Based on the concept plan images:

**Access points:**
- **Primary:** Driveway from Cameron Road (north side of site)
- **Secondary:** Access from the west/southwest connecting to the Pecan Springs Road area

**Fire lane routing observed on concept plan:**
- The fire lane enters from Cameron Road, runs along the **west side** of the building, curves around the **south side** through the parking area, and continues along the **east side** past the dumpster enclosure.
- This creates a roughly U-shaped or three-sided fire lane wrapping west-south-east around the building.

**Coverage analysis:**
- **North face (Cameron Rd side):** The driveway approach from Cameron Road and the potential ROW dedication area place the north face of the building approximately 60-80 ft from the Cameron Road curb line. If the driveway/drive aisle from Cameron Road qualifies as fire lane, this face is adequately served. However, the preliminary pond between the building and Cameron Road may create an obstruction for hose lay measurement. The fire lane line type should extend along the north face or the hose lay path from the nearest fire lane segment around the pond must be confirmed to be within 200 ft (sprinklered).
- **West face:** Directly served by the fire lane running along the western side. Appears compliant.
- **South face:** Served by the fire lane/drive aisle through the parking area. Appears compliant.
- **East face:** The fire lane continues past the dumpster enclosure on the east side. The building's eastern face is approximately 15-20 ft from the east property line. Fire lane routing along this face is tight but appears shown on the plan.

**Potential risk areas:**
1. **Northeast corner:** The CWQZ boundaries, CEF setback lines, and preliminary pond in the NE quadrant of the site may limit fire lane access to the northeast building corner. The hose lay distance from the nearest fire lane segment to the NE corner of the building should be verified to be within 200 ft (measured around obstructions).
2. **Site width constraint:** The lot is approximately 162 ft N-S, and the building plus fire lane, parking, and maneuvering consume most of this dimension. The 25-ft fire lane width requirement, combined with the truck-turn note indicating 35-40 ft is needed for delivery truck maneuvering, creates a tight condition south of the building.

### Fire Lane Width

| Requirement | Standard | Code Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Two-way fire lane | 25 ft minimum | IFC 503.2.1 |
| One-way non-dead-end | 20 ft minimum | IFC 503.2.1 |
| Vertical clearance | 14 ft minimum | IFC 503.2.1 |

The concept plan does not dimension the fire lane width. Site plan must call out 25-ft minimum width at all fire lane segments, with 14-ft vertical clearance confirmed (including under any overhead power lines). No overhead power lines are visible on the concept plan within the fire lane routing, but this must be verified (REQ-02).

### Turning Radii

Fire lane turns require **50-ft outside / 25-ft inside turning radii** (IFC 503.2.4). The concept plan shows what appear to be 10-ft radius curves at certain corners (the crop images show "R10'" callouts at the northeast driveway). These **do not meet** the 50/25 requirement and must be revised at site plan. All turning radii along fire lanes, including the Cameron Road entrance, must be called out and dimensioned (REQ-03).

### Dead-End Fire Lanes

If the fire lane terminates at the east side of the building without a through-connection, it would constitute a dead end. Dead-end fire lanes cannot exceed **150 ft** without an approved turnaround per IFC 503.2.5 and Fire Criteria Manual Appendix G (REQ-04). The concept plan should be evaluated for whether the fire lane forms a through-route (west-to-south-to-east with egress) or a dead end requiring a turnaround.

Based on the concept plan, the fire lane appears to form a loop or through-route with access at both the Cameron Road driveway and the southwest access point. If both access points connect to fire lanes, no dead-end turnaround is required. This must be confirmed at site plan.

### Fire Lane Surface and Loading

Fire lanes must be asphalt or concrete, rated for **HS-20 loading** (32,000 lb/axle, 80,000 lb gross), with maximum grades of 13% (asphalt) or 15% (concrete) and maximum grade change of 10% in 20 ft (REQ-05). The site has a gentle slope (approximately 4-6 ft grade change across the site, per contour lines 626-636), so grades are unlikely to be an issue. The pavement section detail must state HS-20 loading on the site plan drawings.

### Fire Lane Markings and Signage

The site plan must include (REQ-07):
- Fire lane line type on all fire lane segments
- "FIRE ZONE/TOW-AWAY ZONE" stenciled in white letters at least 3 inches high at 35-ft intervals along the curb
- Signs per COA Standard Detail 901S-6 at both ends and every 50 ft or less
- Sign height 5-8 ft above grade

---

## 4. Fire Hydrant Coverage

### Primary Hydrant Distance

| Condition | Maximum Distance | Code Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Non-sprinklered | 400 ft from hydrant to all exterior wall points | IFC 507.5.1 |
| Sprinklered (NFPA 13) | 500 ft from hydrant to all exterior wall points | IFC 507.5.1 |

Distance is measured as hose lay at ground level, not through buildings or across divided highways.

### Existing Hydrant Locations

The concept plan legend includes an "Existing Fire Hydrant" symbol, but no existing fire hydrant is clearly visible on or immediately adjacent to the subject parcel in the concept plan images. The existing 36-inch water main along Cameron Road is expected to serve multiple fire hydrants along the corridor.

**Assessment:** The nearest existing public fire hydrant must be identified and its distance to all portions of the building exterior measured. Given the building footprint of approximately 75 ft x 98 ft (7,375 SF), the maximum diagonal from corner to corner is roughly 124 ft. If a hydrant exists within approximately 375 ft of the nearest building corner (for a sprinklered building), the most remote building point will be within 500 ft.

**If no existing hydrant is within range:** A new private or public hydrant will need to be installed. If private, this triggers TRG-03 (hydraulic calculations sealed by TX PE, NFPA 24 notes, "all private hydrants shall be painted red" note).

### Hydrant Location Requirements (REQ-10)

Any fire hydrant (existing or proposed) serving this site must:
- Be directly adjacent to the fire lane or public street
- Have the steamer (4-inch) opening facing fire access
- Be set back 3-6 ft from curb line
- Have 3 ft clear in all directions
- Not be within the building collapse zone (40 ft from building corner)
- Not be located in pond slopes or detention areas (the preliminary pond area is not a suitable hydrant location)

---

## 5. Fire Department Connection (FDC)

If an NFPA 13 sprinkler system is installed (expected), an FDC is required (REQ-23):

| Requirement | Standard | Code Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Location | Street side of building, fully visible from street or fire lane | IFC 912.2.1 |
| Orientation | Must face designated fire lane (Austin local amendment) | IFC 912.3 |
| Clear area | 3 ft clear around FDC | IFC 912.2.1 |
| Proximity to hydrant | Within 100 ft of hydrant (for standpipe FDC); no specific distance for sprinkler-only FDC, but adjacency preferred | NFPA 14-6.4.5.4 |

**Recommended FDC placement:** The FDC should be located on the **north face** of the building (Cameron Road side), facing the fire lane/driveway from Cameron Road. This provides maximum visibility for responding apparatus and proximity to the public water main. If the north face is not feasible due to the preliminary pond and CWQZ, the **west face** facing the western fire lane is the second-best option.

The FDC location must be shown on both the site plan and utility plan at site plan submittal.

---

## 6. Fire Line, PIV, and Riser Room

### Fire Line Sizing (REQ-18)

For an NFPA 13 sprinkler system, the underground fire line must be a minimum of **6 inches** unless calculations from a licensed sprinkler designer justify a smaller line. The fire line material must be specifically called out (generic "PVC" is not acceptable).

### Post Indicator Valve (REQ-21)

An NFPA 13 system requires one of:
- A **PIV in the underground fire line lead-in**, at least 40 ft from the building, downstream of the backflow preventer; or
- A **wall-mounted PIV**; or
- An **exterior door with direct access to the riser room**

For a single-story AutoZone prototype, the most practical approach is typically an exterior riser room door with a Knox box, eliminating the need for a freestanding PIV.

### Fire Line Notes (REQ-19)

The utility plan must include the standard NFPA 13 fire line note: "Underground mains feeding NFPA 13 sprinkler systems must be installed and tested in accordance with NFPA 13, and the Fire Code, by a licensed sprinkler contractor with a plumbing permit. The entire main must be hydrostatically tested at one time, unless isolation valves are provided between tested sections."

### Riser Room (REQ-38)

The fire riser room location must be shown on both site and utility plans. The fire line entry point must match the riser room location. A Knox box is required at the riser room exterior door (REQ-39).

---

## 7. Dumpster Separation (REQ-31)

The concept plan shows a **proposed dumpster enclosure on the east side** of the building. Per IFC 304.3.3, dumpsters of 1.5 cubic yards or greater shall not be stored within 10 ft of combustible walls, openings, or roof eave lines.

**Assessment:** The dumpster appears to be approximately 10-15 ft from the east building wall based on the concept plan layout. At site plan, the exact dimension must be verified to confirm the 10-ft minimum separation from any combustible wall, opening, or roof eave line. If the building is sprinklered (expected), an exception applies for areas protected by the sprinkler system; however, the dumpster is **exterior** to the building and the sprinkler exception may not extend to exterior dumpster locations.

**Action Required:** Dimension the dumpster enclosure location relative to the nearest building wall/opening and verify >= 10 ft separation, or demonstrate the exception applies.

---

## 8. High-Piled Storage (REQ-34)

The building at 7,375 SF is **below the 12,000 SF threshold** that triggers the AFD high-piled storage review under IFC 3206.2. However, AutoZone stores routinely use racking systems with storage heights exceeding 12 ft. Even though the building is under 12,000 SF, the AFD reviewer may request confirmation of:
- Maximum storage height
- Commodity classification
- Rack type (if any)

This is typically addressed at building permit rather than site plan, but the design team should be prepared to provide this information if requested.

---

## 9. Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI)

**Finding:** The site at 9101 Cameron Rd is in a **fully urbanized commercial corridor** surrounded by existing commercial, industrial, and residential development. The site is **not within the City of Austin Wildland-Urban Interface zone**. WUI zones in Austin are concentrated in the western hills and Barton Springs Zone, not in the northern commercial corridors.

No WUI-related vegetation management plan, ignition-resistant construction, or defensible space requirements apply.

---

## 10. Cover Sheet Requirements (REQ-28, REQ-29, REQ-30)

The site plan must include the following AFD-specific items:

### AFD Information Table (Cover Sheet)

| Field | Required Content |
|---|---|
| Fire Design Codes | 2021 IFC with City of Austin local amendments |
| Fire Flow Demand @ 20 psi | 1,500 gpm (before reductions) |
| Intended Use | Retail Sale of Auto Parts (Group M) |

| AFD Fire Hydrant Flow Test Location | [near point of connection on Cameron Rd] |
| High-Rise | No |
| AMOC | N/A (unless required) |

### Fire Department Notes (REQ-30)

The general notes sheet must include the 7 standard Fire Department Notes exactly as indicated in the current City of Austin Fire Criteria Manual. These cover timing of installations, hydrant installation, HS-20 loading, fire lane registration, and vertical clearance.

### SP Number (REQ-29)

The full site plan number must appear on all sheets.

---

## 11. Cross-Property Access (REQ-37)

The concept plan shows a secondary access point from the west/southwest connecting to the Pecan Springs Road area. If this fire lane access crosses the **west property line** into Block A of the Resubdivision of Cameron Ferguson Park (Housing Authority of the City of Austin property), a **Unified Development Agreement (UDA) or Joint Use Access Easement (JUAE)** would be required (TRG-09).

**Assessment:** The concept plan's western access appears to utilize the existing road network within the Cameron Ferguson Condominiums plat. Because the subject property is Unit 1 of the Cameron Ferguson Condominiums, shared access may already be established through the condominium declaration (Doc. No. 2018119069). However, AFD will require:
- Confirmation that the condominium declaration provides fire lane access rights in perpetuity
- The recording number called out on the plans
- Fire lane boundaries shown on plans within the shared access area

If the condominium declaration does not explicitly provide fire lane access, a separate UDA or JUAE will be needed.

---

## 12. Gates (REQ-27)

No gates across fire lanes are shown on the concept plan. If gates are added during design development, they must comply with IFC 503.6 (Knox key switch for motorized, Knox box for manual, minimum 25-ft width for two-way fire lane gates).

| AFD flow test | Obtain AFD-conducted flow test within 1 year of submittal, both pages, at/near Cameron Rd connection point | High | IFC 507.4 (Local) |
